passages.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, according to the promise of life in Christ Jesus, To Timothy, my beloved child: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter.
Paul is an apostle of Christ Jesus.
God chose Paul to be an apostle.
God did this by His own will.
God promised life in Christ Jesus.
Paul writes to Timothy.
Timothy is Paul's beloved child.
Paul gives a blessing to Timothy.
Paul asks for grace for Timothy.
Paul asks for mercy for Timothy.
Paul asks for peace for Timothy.
These blessings come from God the Father.
These blessings also come from Christ Jesus our Lord.
passages.original: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος Θεοῦ κατ’ ἐπαγγελίαν ζωῆς τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ Τιμοθέῳ ἀγαπητῷ τέκνῳ Χάρις ἔλεος εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν

passages.text: I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience as did my forefathers, as I constantly remember you night and day in my prayers.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter.
Paul is an apostle of Christ Jesus.
God chose Paul to be an apostle.
Paul serves God.
Paul serves God with a clear conscience.
Paul’s forefathers also served God.
Paul thanks God.
Paul remembers Timothy.
Paul remembers Timothy in his prayers.
Paul prays for Timothy night and day.
Paul always remembers Timothy when he prays.
passages.original: Χάριν ἔχω τῷ Θεῷ ᾧ λατρεύω ἀπὸ προγόνων ἐν καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει ὡς ἀδιάλειπτον ἔχω τὴν περὶ σοῦ μνείαν ἐν ταῖς δεήσεσίν μου νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας

passages.text: Recalling your tears, I long to see you so that I may be filled with joy.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy, his beloved child in the faith.
Paul remembers Timothy’s tears.
Paul longs to see Timothy.
Paul wants to be filled with joy by seeing Timothy.
passages.original: ἐπιποθῶν σε ἰδεῖν μεμνημένος σου τῶν δακρύων ἵνα χαρᾶς πληρωθῶ

passages.text: I am reminded of your sincere faith, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am convinced is in you as well.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy.
Paul remembers Timothy’s sincere faith.
This faith is genuine.
This faith first lived in Timothy’s grandmother Lois.
This faith also lived in Timothy’s mother Eunice.
Paul is convinced this same faith now lives in Timothy.
passages.original: ὑπόμνησιν λαβὼν τῆς ἐν σοὶ ἀνυποκρίτου πίστεως ἥτις ἐνῴκησεν πρῶτον ἐν τῇ μάμμῃ σου Λωΐδι καὶ τῇ μητρί σου Εὐνίκῃ πέπεισμαι δὲ ὅτι καὶ ἐν σοί

passages.text: For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy.
Paul is an apostle and a prisoner for Christ.
Timothy is his spiritual child and a faithful believer.
Paul remembers Timothy’s sincere faith.
Paul reminds Timothy of something important.
Paul says, “For this reason, I remind you.”
Paul tells Timothy to fan into flame the gift of God.
God gave this gift to Timothy.
Timothy received this gift through Paul’s laying on of hands.
Paul urges Timothy to keep this gift strong and active.
passages.original: Δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν ἀναμιμνῄσκω σε ἀναζωπυρεῖν τὸ χάρισμα τοῦ Θεοῦ ὅ ἐστιν ἐν σοὶ διὰ τῆς ἐπιθέσεως τῶν χειρῶν μου

passages.text: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
passages.sermon:
God has not given us a spirit of fear.
God has given us a spirit of power.
God has given us a spirit of love.
God has given us a spirit of self-control.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ Θεὸς πνεῦμα δειλίας ἀλλὰ δυνάμεως καὶ ἀγάπης καὶ σωφρονισμοῦ

passages.text: So do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, or of me, His prisoner. Instead, join me in suffering for the gospel by the power of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ.
Paul is a prisoner because of Jesus.
Paul speaks to Timothy.
Paul says, “Do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord Jesus.”
Paul says, “Do not be ashamed of me, even though I am His prisoner.”
Paul says, “Share in suffering for the gospel.”
Paul says, “Rely on the power of God.”
passages.original: Μὴ οὖν ἐπαισχυνθῇς τὸ μαρτύριον τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν μηδὲ ἐμὲ τὸν δέσμιον αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ συνκακοπάθησον τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ κατὰ δύναμιν Θεοῦ

passages.text: He has saved us and called us to a holy calling, not because of our works, but by His own purpose and by the grace He granted us in Christ Jesus before time began.
passages.sermon:
God saved us.
God called us to a holy calling.
God did not save us because of our works.
God saved us because of His own purpose.
God saved us by His grace.
God gave us this grace in Christ Jesus.
God gave us this grace before time began.
passages.original: τοῦ σώσαντος ἡμᾶς καὶ καλέσαντος κλήσει ἁγίᾳ οὐ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα ἡμῶν ἀλλὰ κατὰ ἰδίαν πρόθεσιν καὶ χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσαν ἡμῖν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ πρὸ χρόνων αἰωνίων

passages.text: And now He has revealed this grace through the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who has abolished death and illuminated the way to life and immortality through the gospel, to which I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher.
passages.sermon:
God has now revealed His grace.
He revealed it through the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus.
Christ Jesus is our Savior.
Christ Jesus abolished death.
Christ Jesus brought light to life and immortality.
He did this through the gospel.
God appointed me to serve the gospel.
God made me a preacher.
God made me an apostle.
God made me a teacher.
passages.original: φανερωθεῖσαν δὲ νῦν διὰ τῆς ἐπιφανείας τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ καταργήσαντος μὲν τὸν θάνατον φωτίσαντος δὲ ζωὴν καὶ ἀφθαρσίαν διὰ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου εἰς ὃ ἐτέθην ἐγὼ κήρυξ καὶ ἀπόστολος καὶ διδάσκαλος

passages.text: For this reason, even though I suffer as I do, I am not ashamed; for I know whom I have believed, and I am convinced that He is able to guard what I have entrusted to Him for that day.
passages.sermon:
I suffer because of this reason.
I am not ashamed.
I know whom I have believed.
I am convinced He is able to guard what I have entrusted to Him.
He will guard it until that day.
passages.original: Δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν καὶ ταῦτα πάσχω ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐπαισχύνομαι οἶδα γὰρ ᾧ πεπίστευκα καὶ πέπεισμαι ὅτι δυνατός ἐστιν τὴν παραθήκην μου φυλάξαι εἰς ἐκείνην τὴν ἡμέραν

passages.text: Hold on to the pattern of sound teaching you have heard from me, with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to Timothy.
Paul is an apostle and teacher of Jesus Christ.
Paul tells Timothy to keep a pattern.
This pattern is of sound teaching.
Timothy heard this teaching from Paul.
Timothy must hold to this teaching.
Timothy must do this with faith.
Timothy must do this with love.
This faith and love are in Christ Jesus.
passages.original: Ὑποτύπωσιν ἔχε ὑγιαινόντων λόγων ὧν παρ’ ἐμοῦ ἤκουσας ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Guard the treasure entrusted to you, with the help of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to Timothy.
Paul was a servant of Jesus Christ.
Paul told Timothy to guard something valuable.
This valuable thing is a treasure entrusted to Timothy.
The Holy Spirit lives in us.
The Holy Spirit helps us.
Guard the treasure with the help of the Holy Spirit.
passages.original: τὴν καλὴν παραθήκην φύλαξον διὰ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου τοῦ ἐνοικοῦντος ἐν ἡμῖν

passages.text: You know that everyone in the Province of Asia has deserted me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
passages.sermon:
You know this fact.
Everyone in the Province of Asia has deserted me.
Phygelus has deserted me.
Hermogenes has deserted me.
passages.original: Οἶδας τοῦτο ὅτι ἀπεστράφησάν με πάντες οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ ὧν ἐστιν Φύγελος καὶ Ἑρμογένης

passages.text: May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he has often refreshed me and was unashamed of my chains.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is merciful.
I ask the Lord to show mercy to the household of Onesiphorus.
Onesiphorus often refreshed me.
He was not ashamed of my chains.
passages.original: Δῴη ἔλεος ὁ Κύριος τῷ Ὀνησιφόρου οἴκῳ ὅτι πολλάκις με ἀνέψυξεν καὶ τὴν ἅλυσίν μου οὐκ ἐπαισχύνθη

passages.text: Indeed, when he arrived in Rome, he searched diligently until he found me.
passages.sermon: Onesiphorus came to Rome.\r\nHe searched for me with great effort.\r\nHe found me.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ γενόμενος ἐν Ῥώμῃ σπουδαίως ἐζήτησέν με καὶ εὗρεν

passages.text: May the Lord grant Onesiphorus His mercy on that day. You know very well how much he ministered to me in Ephesus.
passages.sermon: Onesiphorus helped me in Ephesus.\r\nYou know this very well.\r\nI ask the Lord to show mercy to Onesiphorus on that day.
passages.original: Δῴη αὐτῷ ὁ Κύριος εὑρεῖν ἔλεος παρὰ Κυρίου ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ὅσα ἐν Ἐφέσῳ διηκόνησεν βέλτιον σὺ γινώσκεις
